text.title: MLP Planning Core Rules
text.summary: Four-layer Minimum Lovable Product audit (Functional -> Reliable -> Usable -> Delightful) for evolving an MVP that users call 'fine' into one they love and recommend. The four-layer model that defines the path from a functional MVP to a Minimum Lovable Product, with a rating scale and MLP threshold rule.

section.title: Background
section.p: Minimum Lovable Product is the smallest version that delivers core value, creates emotional connection, and gives users a reason to stay and recommend. MLP = MVP + delight. Not more features — better experience.

MVP vs MLP. MVP goal is to validate; MLP goal is to retain. MVP focus is functionality; MLP focus is experience. MVP emotion is "it works"; MLP emotion is "I love it". Word-of-mouth is unlikely from MVP users and likely from MLP users.

rule.statement: MLP plan MUST audit all four layers (Functional, Reliable, Usable, Delightful) and assign a score 0-5 per layer with cited evidence (metric or quote).

rationale.source: Aarron Walter — Designing for Emotion; Henrik Kniberg MLP essay

rule.rationale: Single-layer focus on broken Functional/Reliable layers wastes budget; full audit prevents top-of-pyramid investment on a shaky base.

rule.statement: Delight investments are forbidden when Functional or Reliable score < 3. Fix the base first.

rationale.source: Maslow-style needs hierarchy applied to product

rule.rationale: Delight on a buggy product amplifies frustration; users notice polish on broken flows more, not less.

rule.statement: Delight items MUST cite verbatim user quotes or moment-of-truth observations, not designer opinion.
rule.rationale: Designer-opinion delight ships features the team loves and users don't notice.

rule.statement: MLP success metric is the Day-30 retention curve, not feature throughput. The plan MUST define the curve target before sprint kickoff.

rationale.source: Andrew Chen — Mobile App Retention research

rule.rationale: Without a curve target, MLP work shows up as activity, not impact.

rule.statement: Each delight sprint MUST be <=2 weeks with a single named theme (onboarding, empty-state, completion). Open-ended delight work decays into polish-by-vibe.
rule.rationale: Open-ended delight backlogs accumulate but ship slowly; bounded sprints force scope and ship-rate.

rule.statement: MLP is declared reached only when every core feature scores 4 or higher on all four layers. Any feature below 4 on any layer is an open gap and blocks the declaration.
rule.rationale: The threshold is sufficiency, not perfection; without a numeric bar 'lovable' stays subjective and the team never agrees it has been reached.

rule.statement: Delight backlog MUST be ordered by user pain × frequency × visibility; a delight item on a rarely-seen flow may not outrank one on the daily core action.
rule.rationale: Polish on a screen most users never reach is invisible; the same effort on the core daily action compounds across every session.

rule.statement: Every layer must be solid before adding the next. Delight built on unreliable foundations is wasted.
rule.rationale: Users notice inconsistency before they notice charm. A delightful animation on a crashy flow increases frustration, not affection.

rule.statement: Layer 1 — Functional: core job completes, no blocking bugs, acceptable performance.
rule.rationale: MVP baseline. Without this, nothing else matters.

rule.statement: Layer 2 — Reliable: consistent experience, error handling, edge cases covered, works as expected every time.
rule.rationale: Reliability is the prerequisite for trust. Users forgive a rough UI; they do not forgive data loss or silent failures.

rule.statement: Layer 3 — Usable: easy to learn, efficient to use, minimal friction, good defaults.
rule.rationale: Usability reduces the cognitive tax per session. High friction kills retention even when the product works perfectly.

rule.statement: Layer 4 — Delightful: emotional satisfaction, surprising moments, premium feel, shareable moments.
rule.rationale: Delight creates word-of-mouth and emotional attachment that purely functional products cannot generate.

rule.statement: Rate each core feature 1–5 on each layer. MLP threshold: all features at 4+ on all four layers.
rule.rationale: The threshold is not perfection (5) but sufficiency (4). Rating below 4 on any layer signals a gap that blocks MLP readiness.

rule.statement: For each core feature, rate 1–5 on all four layers. Any feature below 4 on any layer is a gap that must be closed before declaring MLP.
rule.rationale: The audit makes the gap visible and concrete, replacing "the UX needs work" with specific layer deficits per feature.

rule.statement: Scan four moments for delight: first impression (onboarding), core action (the main thing users do), success moments (when they win), and recovery moments (when things go wrong).
rule.rationale: Delight in error states is disproportionately memorable — it converts frustration into loyalty. Most products ignore this.

rule.statement: Apply the formula: polish priority = user pain × frequency × visibility. Only invest in high-frequency, high-visibility interactions.
rule.rationale: Polish on a rarely-seen screen is invisible to most users. The same effort on the daily core action compounds across every session.

rule.statement: Write explicit MLP criteria for your target user segment covering all four layers with measurable outcomes. Template: "For [user segment] MLP means: [functional criteria], [reliable criteria], [usable criteria], [delightful criteria]. Measured by: [verification method]."
rule.rationale: Without explicit criteria, MLP becomes subjective and the team will never agree it has been reached.

rule.statement: For each feature, document: current state, MLP target, what is missing, and effort. This becomes the MLP backlog.
rule.rationale: The gap analysis converts the audit rating into actionable tasks with known scope.

rule.statement: If applicability conditions fail (any Skip-If trigger holds — pre-MVP without Functional shipped; commodity competing on price; B2B with buyer != user; Day-30 retention already >40%), the agent MUST skip this methodology and route to the named alternative or to the methodology fallback.
rule.rationale: Mis-applying a methodology outside its preconditions degrades output quality and pollutes downstream artefacts; the explicit skip-rule keeps the routing tree honest.
